title: Committee of Supply ‒ Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply ‒ Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: Singapore economy ageing workforce limits
sections.summary: Singapore's economy grew about 2% as population ageing and workforce limits mean the economy will soon reach full potential without new capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the midst of these developments, domestically for Singapore, our economy started to grow at a more mature pace of about 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our population entered into a steeper rate of ageing and we are nearing the limits of the growth of our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In other words, we will soon reach the full potential of the economy unless we add new capacity and capabilities again and create new growth drivers.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps essential undertakings
sections.summary: Strengthening linkages, skills, enterprise capabilities, digital economy and Industry Transformation Maps are essential to transform the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Whether it is about strengthening Singapore's international linkages, deepening individual skills, enhancing enterprises' capabilities, building a digital economy, the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) or working together in new ways, these are not unexpected undertakings but are absolutely essential to transform the economy.

sections.label: ITM stakeholders alignment common purpose
sections.summary: Bringing industry stakeholders into the ITM platform harnesses collective wisdom, but ITMs succeed only if stakeholders are aligned to a common purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By bringing into the ITM platform relevant stakeholders of the industries, we could harness the collective wisdom of the industries to drive growth and opportunities and leverage the mutual resources and support to overcome challenges and build new capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But ITMs can only succeed if each of the stakeholders ‒ enterprises, the trade associations and chambers (TACs), labour and agencies ‒ are aligned to a common purpose, and almost altruistic about it.

sections.label: Enterprise spirit, openness, urban solutions, TACs
sections.summary: A value-creating economy should have less Government and more enterprise spirit, though openness brings vulnerability; urban solutions and TACs are also noted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the sort of economy that we envisaged where we gear towards value-creating, innovation and more entrepreneurship, there should actually be less of Government and more of the spirit of enterprise, as what the Minister for Finance said yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Government can help, but the Government may not always make the right business call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But that will also make us more vulnerable to global trends and changes, such as the US withdrawal from the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) and Brexit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How will this strategy of remaining open and connected serve us well, given the rise of anti-globalisation sentiments globally?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thirdly, urban solutions were identified as one of the growth sectors that would benefit from the rising middle-class and urbanisation in Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Fourthly, TACs are critical partners in supporting industry transformation.

sections.label: CFE report medium-term growth target
sections.summary: The CFE report recognises challenges and sets a 2%-3% medium-term growth aim, lower than the 5% previously usual, with 2016 growth at 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: The report produced by CFE recognises these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: It also says that we can aim for 2%-3% growth in the medium term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: However, this is quite a bit lower than the 5% that we were used to for many years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: In 2016, we grew at 2% which, as the Minister for Finance has observed, is at the lower end of the 2%-3% target referred to by CFE, even though it is still in line with the medium-term projections.

sections.label: 2016 growth and 2017 forecast
sections.summary: Singapore's economy grew 2% in 2016 on electronics and biomedical manufacturing, and MTI forecasts 1% to 3% growth with global growth picking up slightly in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, the Singapore economy grew by 2% in 2016, boosted by a better than expected fourth quarter performance from a rebound in the electronics and biomedical manufacturing clusters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) has forecasted that the economy is likely to grow between 1% and 3% and global growth is expected to pick up slightly in 2017.

sections.label: SME cost pressures
sections.summary: SMEs face cost pressures including water price, diesel tax and JTC land rent increases.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) today are faced with a number of cost pressures, from the water price increase, diesel tax increase, annual JTC land rent adjustments and so on.

sections.label: Government infrastructure works brought forward
sections.summary: The Government will bring forward $700 million of infrastructure works in the next two years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: During this economic slowdown, many companies do rely on Government jobs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I am sure the Minister of State's announcement that the Government will bring forward $700 million of infrastructure works in the next two years will be welcomed by the construction industry.

sections.label: Study to consolidate regulations
sections.summary: A study is proposed to identify and consolidate regulations while protecting public interests and safety.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: But surely, there must be cost efficiencies if we scrutinise and optimise the myriad of regulations that is imposed by agencies today.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to propose that we initiate a study to identify and consolidate regulations while ensuring that we continue to protect and guard the interests and safety of the public.

sections.label: SBF disappointed with Budget support
sections.summary: The SBF said it was disappointed with inadequate short-term support to lower business costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After this year's Budget was delivered, the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) said it was disappointed with the inadequate short-term support to lower business costs, including "the absence of measures on rental rebates for businesses in general." Why is that?

sections.label: Targeted rental rebates for SMEs
sections.summary: The Ministry could consider targeted rental rebates for qualifying SMEs, startups or microbusinesses in certain sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry consider whether targeted assistance, for example, rental rebates directed at qualifying SMEs or startups in certain sectors may be feasible, say, to stimulate retail-oriented SMEs, startups or microbusinesses, so as to bring added diversity and vibrancy to our heartlands?

sections.label: Business rental cost benchmarking study
sections.summary: A comprehensive historical and international benchmarking study on business rental costs is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, rental of premises was found to be the second factor with the greatest impact on profitability, coming in after manpower costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Even though concerns over rental have finally dipped slightly in 2016 owing to slower growth overall, this is a problem that we must still pay close attention to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will consider conducting a major comprehensive historical and international benchmarking study on business rental costs to understand why rental costs rose so rapidly over the past two decades and why, despite the Government's efforts in recent years to release more land through the Industrial Government Land Sales (IGLS) programme so as to ensure more industrial space, SMEs are still feeling the squeeze.

sections.label: Supporting workers and industry
sections.summary: It asks whether Government measures to support the sector have succeeded and how success is determined.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It makes it harder for the industry to pick up again when the economy and the sector improve, so it is all the more important that we help our workers, that we help our brothers and sisters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, can the Ministry advise whether the Government's measures to support the sector have been successful?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: What measures does the Government use to determine success?

sections.label: China monetary and fiscal policies
sections.summary: In China, expansionary monetary and fiscal policies supported 6.7% GDP growth in 2016, its slowest in 26 years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Similarly, in China, expansionary monetary and fiscal policies supported their growth with 6.7% GDP in 2016, but it is their slowest in 26 years.

sections.label: Global trade and FTAs
sections.summary: Global trade grew over two decades, and Singapore's FTA network gave preferential market access and trade linkages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Global trade has grown significantly in the last two decades, supported by global trade liberalisation and the proliferation of global value chains and rising incomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Our network of FTAs has given us preferential access to key markets, stronger trade linkages with our FTA partners and opened up opportunities for our companies.

sections.label: Trade and globalisation politicised
sections.summary: The CFE report says trade and globalisation have become politicised, blamed for income inequality and poor job creation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the report of CFE has pointed out, trade and globalisation have become more politicised, as they are blamed for rising income inequality or the inability to create good jobs.

sections.label: Protectionism and MTI openness
sections.summary: With signs of rising protectionism among G20 economies, it asks what MTI is doing to keep Singapore and partners open.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Much depends on what the major economies will do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: There are also signs of increasing protectionism amongst the G20 economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: In this challenging climate, what is MTI doing to ensure that Singapore and its key trade partners stay open and connected?

sections.label: Global economic outlook 2017
sections.summary: Global growth is expected to remain modest in 2017, picking up slightly to 3.4% from 3.1% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Foo Mee Har asked about the global economic outlook and the implications for the Singapore economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We expect global growth to remain modest in 2017, with growth projected to pick up slightly to 3.4%, from 3.1% in 2016.

sections.label: GDP growth 2016 and 2017
sections.summary: GDP growth was 2% in 2016, and growth in 2017 is expected to be similar barring downside risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: GDP growth came in at 2% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Barring downside risks, we expect growth in 2017 to be similar to 2016.

sections.label: Labour productivity growth 2010-2016
sections.summary: Overall labour productivity grew at a modest pace of 1.5% per annum from 2010 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Overall labour productivity grew at a modest pace of 1.5% per annum from 2010 to 2016.

sections.label: EDB investment commitments averages
sections.summary: Over the past five years, EDB's investment commitments brought in an average of S$12 billion in fixed asset investment and S$7 billion in total business expenditure annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, the Economic Development Board's (EDB's) investment commitments have brought in an average of S$12 billion in fixed asset investment and S$7 billion in total business expenditure annually.

sections.label: SME Working Capital Loan
sections.summary: The SME Working Capital Loan allows SMEs unsecured working capital of up to $300,000, and by end-2016 over $700 million and 4,800 loans benefited around 4,300 SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: One initiative is the SME Working Capital Loan, which allows SMEs to access unsecured working capital of up to $300,000 and complements existing financial schemes to support our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: As at the end of 2016, more than $700 million and 4,800 loans have been catalysed, benefiting around 4,300 SMEs.

sections.label: M&OE financing schemes
sections.summary: In November last year, the M&OE Bridging Loan was introduced and the M&OE Internationalisation Finance Scheme enhanced to facilitate access to working capital and financing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: In November last year, we introduced the Marine and Offshore Engineering (M&OE) Bridging Loan and enhanced the M&OE Internationalisation Finance Scheme to facilitate M&OE companies' access to working capital and financing.

sections.label: Expected loan catalysation
sections.summary: The measures are expected to catalyse about $1.6 billion in loans over one year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: The measures are expected to catalyse about $1.6 billion in loans over one year.

sections.label: Manufacturing unit business cost index
sections.summary: The unit business cost index for the manufacturing sector fell 8.5% from 2015 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: The unit business cost (UBC) index for the manufacturing sector fell 8.5% from 2015 to 2016.

sections.label: Rebates and Capability Development Grant
sections.summary: The Government cannot enforce compelling businesses in return for rebates, so it uses schemes like the Capability Development Grant, which defrays up to 70% of qualifying project costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We cannot compel them to do so in return for the rebates, as such a condition will not be enforceable operationally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Government has other ways to support our businesses, including schemes like the Capability Development Grant, which encourages businesses to build business capabilities by defraying up to 70% of qualifying project costs.

sections.label: Trade and external demand
sections.summary: Trade and external demand are key drivers of the economy, accounting for two-thirds of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Trade and external demand are key drivers of our economy, accounting for two-thirds of our GDP.

sections.label: IE Singapore Internationalisation Survey
sections.summary: IE Singapore's 2016 Internationalisation Survey showed overseas revenue grew 4.2% year-on-year, compared to total revenue growth of 1.3% year-on-year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: International Enterprise (IE) Singapore's 2016 Internationalisation Survey showed that our companies' overseas revenue grew 4.2% year-on-year, compared to the total revenue growth of 1.3% year-on-year.

sections.label: Leveraging trade agreements and FTAs
sections.summary: Singapore has 21 FTAs with 32 trading partners, which helped companies benefit from over $900 million in tariff savings in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: First, we must continue to leverage our trade agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We have a network of 21 FTAs with 32 trading partners in multiple regions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: These agreements helped our companies to benefit from tariff savings of over $900 million in 2015.

sections.label: AC Global Energy technology acquisition
sections.summary: AC Global Energy acquired technology from their US partner to convert pine wood to green diesel, biochar and wood vinegar, and operates a biodiesel plant in Tennessee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: For example, AC Global Energy acquired technology from their US partner to convert pine wood to green diesel, biochar and wood vinegar.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: They currently operate a biodiesel plant in Tennessee and are looking to build another plant in Alabama.

sections.label: Kino Biotech e-commerce China
sections.summary: Kino Biotech, an SME selling healthcare products, uses e-commerce with IE Singapore's assistance to enter the Chinese market via Alibaba's Tmall.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Kino Biotech, an SME which sells healthcare products, such as collagen drinks, is using e-commerce to augment its internationalisation efforts to enter the Chinese market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: With IE Singapore's assistance, Kino Biotech began listing their products on Alibaba's Tmall Singapore Shop in 2016 and found e-commerce to be an effective sales channel.

sections.label: InvitroCue Qiagen Suzhou collaboration
sections.summary: Since August last year, InvitroCue has collaborated with Qiagen Suzhou to jointly develop, brand and market new technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Since August last year, InvitroCue has collaborated with Qiagen Suzhou, a joint venture between Dutch MNC Qiagen and Suzhou Industrial Park Biotechnology Development, to jointly develop, brand and market new technologies.

sections.label: ITMs under 2016 Budget programme
sections.summary: ITMs were part of the $4.5 billion 2016 Budget programme for growth, competitiveness and jobs in 23 industries, with six launched and 17 more expected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: Chairman, ITMs were part of the $4.5 billion programme announced in the 2016 Budget aimed at promoting growth, helping companies become more competitive and creating good jobs in 23 industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: Six ITMs have been launched so far, with 17 more expected to be launched this year.

sections.label: TACs, LEAD+ and ITM priorities
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether ITM efforts should be prioritised, what impact LEAD+ had on TACs, and cites Germany, Korea and Taiwan as examples.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: It is encouraging that, rather than pick winners, MTI has chosen to build industry-level capabilities for all 23 sectors concurrently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: But given our limited resources and the executional complexity in implementing these ITMs, would it not be more prudent to prioritise our efforts on industries with high-growth potential and well-established sector partnership structures?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: During last year's Committee of Supply (COS) debate, I pointed out that TACs need to step up to their role and there is much that is expected of them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: So, what impact, I would like to ask the Minister, the new Local Enterprise and Association Development-Plus (LEAD+) programme had in helping TACs improve their outreach, attract talent, develop their capabilities and strengthen their processes and services?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: Could the Minister share some good examples of how selected TACs have been successful in leading the development of industry-wide transformation and helping their members to make inroads overseas?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: We really need to learn from countries with strong trade associations, such as Germany, Korea and Taiwan, on how their TACs have helped their industries raise productivity, invest in jobs and skills, leverage research and development (R&D), promote the adoption of technology and form formidable consortiums to capture overseas business.

sections.label: Firms navigating uncertain environment
sections.summary: Working on potential parameters and eliminating potentials helps firms make sense of an uncertain environment, a decline from earlier years as alternate locations surfaced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Working on those potential parameters and eliminating potentials along the way is, in itself, helping firms make sense of an uncertain environment and helping them feel their way forward.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: This is a decline from earlier years as alternate cost competitive locations surfaced and availability of industry resources improved in emerging markets.

sections.label: ITMs coordinate policies across agencies
sections.summary: ITMs aim to coordinate policies from different agencies for each of the 23 industries covered by the Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: To this end, ITMs aim to coordinate policies from different agencies for each of the 23 industries covered by the Government's Industry Transformation Programme.

sections.label: R&D investment and economic outcomes
sections.summary: The Government has invested significantly in R&D, including $19 billion under RIE2020, and wants structures and policies so investments lead to positive economic outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: The Government has made significant investments in R&D over the years, including the latest $19 billion investment under RIE2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: It is important to ensure that we have structures and policies in place, so that our R&D investments can lead to positive economic outcomes.

sections.label: A*STAR role in innovation system
sections.summary: A*STAR bridges academia and industry and partners enterprises to transfer and co-develop technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: A*STAR plays an important role in our innovation system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: It bridges the gap between academia and industry, and partners enterprises across the spectrum to transfer and co-develop technologies.

sections.label: Components of intellectual capital
sections.summary: Intellectual capital comprises human capital, intellectual assets and intellectual property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Intellectual capital comprises human capital, intellectual assets and intellectual property.

sections.label: National innovation vision and structural reforms
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for a mindset change in agencies, asks whether Singapore has an overarching national innovation vision, and wants details of structural reforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But even so, I hope that we will see a true mindset change in the relevant agencies, and not just cosmetic changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope to be enlightened as to whether Singapore has crafted an overarching national innovation vision to steer our innovation policies to support national and institutional innovation programmes and projects and to provide the framework by which we would assess our performance against what we intend to achieve under our national innovation vision and how they compare with others globally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope we will move away from an "ownself clap ownself" assessment approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand there will be structural reforms, I would like to know what the structural reforms are and will entail.

sections.label: Economic multipliers of R&D spending
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry studies and publishes economic multipliers resulting from public R&D spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Aside from the published data for the public R&D sector like employees, projects, patents, startup numbers, R&D spending and so on, does the Ministry study and publish the economic multipliers resulting from this spending?

sections.label: Jobs generated from IP
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry has a count of jobs directly or indirectly generated from that IP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, does the Ministry also have a count of jobs that are directly or indirectly generated from that IP?

sections.label: Possible electricity price rise
sections.summary: The announcement has spurred talk of up to a 4.3% rise in electricity prices for downstream consumers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The announcement has spurred talk that this could result in up to a 4.3% rise in electricity prices for downstream consumers.

sections.label: Singapore renewable energy targets
sections.summary: Singapore aims for 10% renewable energy by 2025, with carbon tax offsets and solar power adoption plans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, only 4% of electricity in Singapore is produced from sources other than natural gas and petroleum.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should aim for 10% renewable energy production by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will put us on par with other small developed countries like South Korea which has a target of 7% by 2020 and Belgium, with 13%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To provide incentives for power stations and other large emitters to turn to renewables, the Government should link the investment and use of renewable energy to carbon tax offsets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: Chairman, there has been a growing interest in sustainability following our ratification of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: We have pledged to reduce our carbon emission per dollar of GDP by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: In his Budget Speech, Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat mentioned that a carbon tax will be levied starting from 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: One of our plans to reduce our carbon footprint is to raise the adoption of solar power to 350-megawatt peak (MWp) by 2020, which represents 5% of peak electricity demand.

sections.label: Proposed carbon tax electricity impact
sections.summary: The National Climate Change Secretariat said the proposed tax rate equals a 0.43 to 0.86 cents per kWh rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: The National Climate Change Secretariat said that this proposed tax rate is equivalent to a rise in electricity prices of between 0.43 and 0.86 cents per kilowatt-hour (kWh).

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: It also stated that this could mean between 2.1% and 4.3% increase in electricity prices compared to current rates.

sections.label: Food manufacturing sector growth targets
sections.summary: The aim is to grow food manufacturing value-add, overseas income and productivity by 2020, with most enterprises being SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The aim is to grow our food manufacturing sector's value-add (VA) by 6.5% per annum, overseas income by 8% per annum, and productivity by 4.5% per annum, by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Ninety-eight percent of the almost 850 food manufacturing enterprises in Singapore are SMEs.

sections.label: SPRING investing in HPP machine
sections.summary: SPRING will invest at least $1.5 million in an HPP machine in Jurong, ready by the fourth quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For example, a typical small juice company with an annual production volume of 40,000 litres, would need such a machine for only about four days in a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, SPRING will be investing at least $1.5 million in such an HPP machine.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This machine will be located in Jurong, where there is a concentration of food manufacturing companies, and it will be ready by the fourth quarter of this year.

sections.label: Aalst productivity projects results
sections.summary: SPRING's Capability Development Grants helped Aalst invest in productivity projects, increasing production capacity by 70%.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: With SPRING's Capability Development Grants, Aalst has invested in a series of productivity projects, including an automated production line to improve the efficiency of chocolate production and packaging.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It helped Aalst increase production capacity by 70%, which allowed it to scale, meet higher export demand without the need to increase manpower.

sections.label: Food Manufacturing Skills Framework
sections.summary: SPRING is working with unions and industry to develop a Food Manufacturing Skills Framework to match skills supply with industry demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To better match skills supply with industry demand, SPRING is working with the unions and industry to develop a Food Manufacturing Skills Framework.

sections.label: Other 17 ITMs launch model
sections.summary: A similar model will be adopted for the other 17 ITMs, to be launched by the end of FY 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I have spoken in detail about the progress of the Food Manufacturing ITM and how it will involve and benefit workers, companies and TACs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We will adopt a similar model for the other 17 ITMs which will be launched by the end of this financial year, meaning financial year (FY) 2017.

sections.label: 23 ITMs GDP share
sections.summary: The 23 ITMs account for about 80% of GDP and will all be launched by the end of the FY.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The 23 ITMs account for about 80% of our GDP and, generally, they meet the kind of criteria that Ms Foo has mentioned, and they will all be launched by the end of the FY, as I have said.

sections.label: HSA priority review scheme
sections.summary: HSA will establish a priority review scheme to allow innovative medical devices quicker access to market.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To allow innovative medical devices to gain quicker access to market, HSA will establish a priority review scheme.

sections.label: Pre-market consultation scheme
sections.summary: HSA will launch a pre-market consultation scheme to give medical device developers greater regulatory certainty.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To give medical device developers greater regulatory certainty, HSA will also launch a "pre-market consultation scheme".

sections.label: Flexible industrial land zoning pilot
sections.summary: JTC, SPRING and URA are working on a flexible industrial land zoning approach, piloted at a JTC building in Woodlands North Coast.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: JTC, SPRING and URA have been working on a more flexible industrial land zoning approach, which will be piloted at a multi-tenanted building to be developed by JTC and located within Woodlands North Coast.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Instead of the "60/40" guideline, JTC will introduce more flexible guidelines so that companies can co-locate service-driven activities alongside their manufacturing operations.

sections.label: Land use flexibility in Punggol
sections.summary: Greater land use flexibility will be piloted at district level in upcoming growth centres, starting with Punggol.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: More broadly, vibrant live-work-play-learn environments also play a growing role in the attraction and retention of talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, beyond flexibility at the development level, we will also pilot greater land use flexibility at the district level in our upcoming growth centres, starting with Punggol.

sections.label: Singapore Centres and GIA
sections.summary: Singapore Centres will extend to 36 overseas locations, and a GIA will be established to help startups build networks and seize export opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Some examples include Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Frankfurt, London and Mumbai.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We will extend the Singapore Centres to all the other 36 overseas locations where EDB and IE Singapore are present.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In addition, as the Minister for Finance has announced, we will establish the GIA, whose objective is to help our startups build networks and seize export opportunities in global innovation hubs and new demand markets.

sections.label: Four research framework domains
sections.summary: The research framework focuses on four domains: advanced manufacturing and engineering, health and biomedical sciences, services and digital economy, and urban solutions and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: First, our research framework is focused on four domains which hold significant economic opportunities and serve important national needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: These are: (a) advanced manufacturing and engineering; (b) health and biomedical sciences; (c) services and digital economy; and (d) urban solutions and sustainability.

sections.label: Open and increased share
sections.summary: It is open rather than dedicated, and has increased from 20% to 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, it is not dedicated; it is open.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And that is increased from 20% to 40%.

sections.label: A*STAR RIE2015 industry outcomes
sections.summary: A*STAR undertook close to 9,000 industry projects, catalysing over S$1.6 billion in industry R&D investments, with spin-offs and follow-on funding increasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In the RIE2015 tranche, A*STAR undertook close to 9,000 industry projects which catalysed more than S$1.6 billion of industry R&D investments in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Around 70% of the licences were with SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In RIE2015, a total of 202 SMEs benefited from the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The number of A*STAR's spin-offs has increased from the S&T2010 to 71 in RIE2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The follow-on funding has also increased from $46 million to $90 million for the same period.

sections.label: National IP Protocol
sections.summary: A National IP Protocol will be created to give companies and public agencies a clear, consistent framework to access publicly-funded IP.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In particular, we will create a National IP Protocol to provide companies and public agencies with a clear and consistent framework to access publicly-funded IP.

sections.label: SPRING SME support budget
sections.summary: SPRING has budgeted $80 million to support SMEs under this programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: SPRING has budgeted $80 million to support SMEs under this programme.

sections.label: Clean energy growth and jobs
sections.summary: The efforts are expected to bring sustainable growth in clean energy, with potentially 2,000 new PMET jobs by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: With these efforts, we expect sustainable growth in our clean energy sector, with more enterprise and job creation, potentially 2,000 new PMET jobs in the sector by 2025.

sections.label: Solar adoption capacity increase
sections.summary: A 2014 plan aimed to raise solar adoption to 350 MWp by 2020, with installed capacity rising from under 20 MWp to 126 MWp.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In 2014, we announced a plan to raise the adoption of solar power in our system to 350 MWp by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Since then, the installed capacity has risen from less than 20 MWp to 126 MWp today.

sections.label: Solar target and climate pledge
sections.summary: EMA concluded one GWp of solar can be accommodated, supporting the 2030 pledge to cut emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Looking beyond 2020, we plan to further raise the adoption of solar power in our system to one gigawatt peak (GWp).

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And noting that the cost of intermittency must be balanced against the cost of carbon emissions, perhaps represented by a carbon tax, EMA has concluded that one GWp of solar can be accommodated in our system.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This will support the achievement of our 2030 climate change pledge to reduce our emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030.

sections.label: Emerging Asia small-scale project demand
sections.summary: Much emerging Asia demand will be for small-scale water, power and renewable projects typically valued between S$5 million and S$70 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And much of the demand in emerging Asia will be for small-scale projects in water and wastewater treatment plants, discrete small scale independent power plants, and renewable energy projects like solar farms and mini-hydro plants.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Such projects range in value typically between S$5 million and about S$70 million.

sections.label: IFS non-recourse financing scheme
sections.summary: The IFS Non-Recourse Financing Scheme has the Government co-share banks' risks on non-recourse loans to SMEs, secured only by project assets and cash flows.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And this makes it difficult for the SMEs to scale up.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is why we have introduced the Internationalisation Finance Scheme (IFS) Non-Recourse Financing Scheme  (Non-recourse Finance), through which the Government will co-share banks' risks in providing non-recourse loans to SMEs for such projects and these non-recourse loans are secured only by the project's assets and its cash flows which will enable SMEs to take on more projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: One, in particular, is to secure loans for large projects undertaken on behalf of the sovereigns of developing countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And these can be for projects involving rail, ports, airports, conventional power plants and desalination plants, and the typical value exceeds half a billion dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Singapore-based developers do not have access to such facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, to help level the playing field for Singapore-based developers, the Government will enhance the existing IFS administered by IE Singapore, to provide insurance against default of payments by sovereigns in selected emerging markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This is an important and measured step in the Government's efforts to help unlock private financing for Singapore-based infrastructure companies and help them secure projects which leverage their capabilities.

sections.label: ITMs as key mechanism
sections.summary: ITMs are a key mechanism, with strategies and programmes adjusted to environmental changes and a proactive regulatory stance adopted.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And ITMs are going to be a key mechanism for us to achieve this.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We will adjust our strategies and programmes in response to changes in our environment and adopt a proactive and forward-looking regulatory stance.

sections.label: SMEs face structural changes
sections.summary: As the economy slows to 1%-3% and online retailers disrupt, many SMEs find it challenging to adapt and compete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: As our economy slows down to 1%-3% in the long run and there are more disruptive changes, such as the onset of online retailers, many SMEs are finding it challenging to adapt to these structural changes and compete effectively.

sections.label: Innovation investment survey findings
sections.summary: Survey findings showed less than one-third of respondents had invested in innovation in the past two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Survey findings revealed that as investing in innovation may not lead to actual outcomes, less than one-third of respondents had invested in innovation over the past two to three years.

sections.label: A*STAR Operation and Technology Road-mapping
sections.summary: The Budget announced A*STAR is scaling up the Operation and Technology Road-mapping initiative to support 400 companies over four years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Budget announced that A*STAR is scaling up on the Operation and Technology Road-mapping initiative, to support 400 companies over the next four years.

sections.label: International Partnership Fund
sections.summary: The Government committed a $600 million International Partnership Fund to help local enterprises invest in overseas markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With regard to internationalisation, the Government has committed a $600 million International Partnership Fund to help local enterprises invest in overseas markets.

sections.label: Public sector infrastructure projects
sections.summary: The Government is bringing forward $700 million worth of public sector infrastructure projects to boost the construction sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One of our delegates, who runs a local construction firm, said: "If we could clinch a substantial project in Singapore, this would give us greater confidence to bid for overseas projects." In order to boost the construction sector, the Government is bringing forward $700 million worth of public sector infrastructure projects.

sections.label: Help for SMEs
sections.summary: MOF gave SMEs tax rebates and employment credit last year, and this year offers more targeted help for efficiency, internationalisation and digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, MOF provided greater help to SMEs, such as more corporate income tax rebate and the extension of the Special Employment Credit scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This year, there are even more targeted help for SMEs to improve their efficiency and go international and digital, with a focus on data analytics and cybersecurity.

sections.label: Retail sector productivity
sections.summary: The latest MTI report shows the retail sector has one of the lowest productivity levels besides construction.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From the latest MTI report, besides the construction sector, the retail sector seems to have one of the lowest in productivity.

sections.label: Revitalisation of Shops scheme
sections.summary: The enhanced Revitalisation of Shops scheme aims to rejuvenate heartland shops, which mostly benefit from improved physical appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Although there is this enhanced Revitalisation of Shops (ROS) scheme aimed at rejuvenating the heartland shops, the shops are mostly benefiting from improved physical appeal.

sections.label: Businesses excluded from grants
sections.summary: Some businesses want to move with the times but, unlike SMEs, are not entitled to grants, rebates, consultation and staff training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Some of these businesses do wish to move with the times but, unlike SMEs and other enterprises, they are not entitled to things like grants, rebates, consultation and staff training.

sections.label: Lift spare parts investigation
sections.summary: The Competition Commission of Singapore announced it was investigating restrictive industry practices in the supply of lift spare parts for Town Council lifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, in the middle of last year, the Competition Commission of Singapore announced that it was investigating restrictive industry practices in the supply of lift spare parts for lifts managed by Town Councils.

sections.label: EM Services supply commitment
sections.summary: EM Services refused to supply spare parts to third-party contractors, then committed to supply EM lift spare parts to third-party maintenance contractors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: EM Services was found to have refused to supply spare parts to third-party contractors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 12 May 2016, some two years after the initial complaint, EM Services came forward to provide a commitment to supply lift spare parts for the lift brand known to most Singaporeans as "EM", to third-party lift maintenance contractors in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Following feedback from a public consultation, the Commission considered EM Services' commitments to fully address competition concerns, presumably concerns which originate from possible breaches of section 47 of the Competition Act.

sections.label: Competition Commission interim orders question
sections.summary: Asks whether the Competition Commission considered interim orders compelling EM Services to sell spare parts to competitor maintenance companies during the investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Did the Competition Commission consider making interim orders against EM Services, so as to compel them to sell spare parts to competitor maintenance companies during the period under investigation?

sections.label: Manufacturing sector and CFE report
sections.summary: The sector diversifies production and exports, and the CFE report recommended retaining manufacturing at around 20% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: The sector also helps to diversify our production base and export markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: I was, therefore, very pleased to note that the report by CFE recommended that Singapore continue building a globally competitive manufacturing sector and should retain manufacturing at around 20% of our GDP over the medium term.

sections.label: Government support for company transformation
sections.summary: Asks how the Government supports companies adopting advanced manufacturing technologies and building new capabilities to seize growth opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: In view of this, how is the Government supporting our companies in their transformation journeys to adopt advanced manufacturing technologies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: How will the Government help our companies build new capabilities so that they can remain relevant and seize new opportunities for growth?

sections.label: Work pass and EntrePass recommendations
sections.summary: A subcommittee recommended reviewing the work pass system for startup founders and executives, and SBF recommended enhancing the EntrePass scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: Given Singapore's small size, one of the subcommittees recommended that the Government review the existing work pass system, so that it is easier for startup founders and key executives to come to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: SBF's SME Committee has similarly recommended that the existing EntrePass scheme be enhanced.

sections.label: Sustaining 1%-3% growth amid globalisation threats
sections.summary: Asks whether 1%-3% growth can be maintained amid threats to globalisation and fewer foreign direct investments, and what more is needed.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: With increasing threats to globalisation and potentially fewer foreign direct investments, can we continue to maintain this growth of 1%-3%?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Apart from short-term measures, what more must we do to sustain a growth on par with or better than the global forecast for advanced economies?

sections.label: Exporting services to emerging markets
sections.summary: Asks whether Singapore can export its services and create job opportunities for Singaporeans in emerging markets.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Instead of just local demand creation, can we export our services and create job opportunities for Singaporeans in emerging markets?

sections.label: New industry sectors and overseas expansion
sections.summary: Asks whether considerations exist to develop new industry sectors and help local companies expand manufacturing overseas across the value chain.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Apart from R&D, are there any considerations to develop new industry sectors and assist our local companies to expand manufacturing overseas where different parts of the entire value chain can be strategically located?

sections.label: Plans to capture talent pool
sections.summary: Asks what plans the Ministry has to capture this talent pool.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: What plans does the Ministry have to capture this talent pool?

sections.label: Entrepreneur's US roadshow and language
sections.summary: An entrepreneur said he only did a US roadshow because he could not present or negotiate in Chinese, and US investors found the company too far away.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: When asked why he had only conducted a roadshow in the US to secure venture capital (VC) funding and not in China, an entrepreneur whose company had created an online portal for services remarked, "I can't do a powerpoint in Chinese and I can't handle negotiations with them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Further, my product is personal computer (PC)-based whereas they are into mobile apps." And when I probed further if he had been successful in raising funding in the US, the entrepreneur replied, "No, the US investors said we were too physically far away and that it would be difficult for them to review how we are doing post-investment".

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If we are looking to crack nearby markets, being able to converse in Chinese or a Southeast Asian language would be helpful.

sections.label: Supporting nearby markets and immersion
sections.summary: Suggests supporting language, cultural studies and immersion programmes in neighbouring countries alongside Government schemes for companies setting up overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Lastly, while we should attempt new and exciting far-flung markets, nearby markets, by value of proximity, allows greater interaction and increases the possibility that business can be done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I suggest that alongside Government schemes to help our companies set up overseas, we should also support language, cultural studies and programmes which offer immersion opportunities in neighbouring countries to young Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This will enable them to understand and create relevant products and services for consumers in the region.

sections.label: 23 ITMs covering economy
sections.summary: States that eventually there will be 23 ITMs covering more than 80% of the economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Eventually, we will have 23 ITMs covering more than 80% of our economy.

sections.label: Self-checkouts and cashier demand
sections.summary: States over 110 self-checkouts were installed in supermarkets in 2016, cutting cashier demand 20%, with a 2020 adoption target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2016, more than 110 self-checkouts were installed in supermarkets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This has allowed a 20% reduction in the demand for cashiers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our target is for 50% of large retailers to adopt these established technologies by 2020.

sections.label: Companies benefiting from classes
sections.summary: 38 companies have benefited from these classes, and more are encouraged to join.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To date, 38 companies have benefited from these classes and we encourage more to join in.

sections.label: Centres assisted enterprises in 2016
sections.summary: In total, the Centres assisted about 30,600 enterprises in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In total, our Centres assisted about 30,600 enterprises in 2016.

sections.label: Tech Depot on SME Portal
sections.summary: A one-stop Tech Depot will be added to the SME Portal by the second quarter of 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To improve our companies' access to technology and digital solutions, we will add a one-stop Tech Depot to the SME Portal by the second quarter of 2017.

sections.label: A*STAR technology roadmaps and facilitators
sections.summary: A*STAR has developed over 240 technology roadmaps since 2003 and aims to support up to 400 companies over four years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Since 2003, A*STAR has developed over 240 technology roadmaps, with positive feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This year, we will partner the trade associations to expand our network of trained OTR facilitators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We aim to support up to 400 companies over the next four years.

sections.label: SMEs took up CDG projects
sections.summary: In 2016, SMEs took up close to 2,400 CDG projects, totaling $125 million in grants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2016, SMEs took up close to 2,400 CDG projects, totaling $125 million in grants.

sections.label: SPRING procurement for innovation
sections.summary: SPRING will work with Government agencies such as HDB and JTC to drive procurement for innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To overcome this, SPRING will be working with several Government agencies, such as HDB and JTC, to drive procurement for innovation.

sections.label: JTC test-bedding with companies
sections.summary: JTC works with companies to fund and test-bed innovative solutions, including flexible solar films with local SME vTrium Energy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As one of the agencies pioneering this, JTC has already been working with companies to fund and test-bed innovative solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It has worked with vTrium Energy, a local SME, on the test-bedding of flexible solar films within its CleanTech Park and Seletar Aerospace Park.

sections.label: CCS interim measures directive
sections.summary: To date, CCS has not issued any interim measures directive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To date, CCS has not issued any interim measures directive.

sections.label: Projects supported with committed grant
sections.summary: Close to 190 of these projects have been supported, with a committed grant of $190 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Altogether, close to 190 of these projects have been supported, with a committed grant of $190 million.

sections.label: LEAD Programme budget increase
sections.summary: The overall FY2016 to 2020 budgets under the LEAD Programme will increase to $100 million to help more TACs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We recognise the importance of TACs as our key partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will increase the overall FY2016 to 2020 budgets under the LEAD Programme to $100 million to help more TACs to step up and do more for their members.

sections.label: Strengthening TACs in ITM sectors
sections.summary: TACs in all 23 ITM sectors will be strengthened, with support up to 90% for cross-sectoral or multi-TAC projects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Second, we will strengthen TACs in all the 23 ITM sectors, so that they can play a stronger role in driving industry transformation and internationalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Cross-sectoral, multi-TACs or projects where larger TACs step up to support smaller ones, can be supported up to 90%, from the current 70%.

sections.label: SME Centres and consultancy services
sections.summary: The Government set up 12 SME Centres and works to enhance their service quality to provide more targeted business consultancy services for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Several Ministers who spoke before me have talked about the short-term and long-to-medium term measures that the Government has rolled out to support SMEs, and how to help SMEs stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It is why the Government has set up 12 SME Centres and have constantly worked to enhance the service quality of these centres, so that they can provide more targeted business consultancy services for SMEs.

sections.label: SME Go-Digital and OTR
sections.summary: The Government will provide more detailed assistance, including the SME Go-Digital Programme and the new OTR Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In this aspect, the Government is happy to provide more detailed assistance, including the SME Go-Digital Programme and the new OTR Scheme.

sections.label: FMAS neighbourhood development plans
sections.summary: FMAS will be supported in formulating new development plans for specific neighbourhoods, starting with Ang Mo Kio and Bedok.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Going forward, we will support FMAS in formulating new development plans for specific neighbourhoods, with Ang Mo Kio and Bedok being the first two to roll out their plans.

sections.label: Manufacturing GDP and employment share
sections.summary: Manufacturing accounts for around 20% of GDP and 14% of employment, and MTI supports retaining it at around 20% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The sector currently accounts for around 20% of our GDP and 14% of total employment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: MTI supports the CFE recommendation to retain manufacturing at around 20% of our GDP in the medium term.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Based on MTI's estimates, a S$1-billion increase in manufacturing value-added through final demand generates about S$330 million of value-added, and 2,500 jobs for the rest of the economy, including business services and wholesale trade.

sections.label: Model Factories at SIMTech and ARTC
sections.summary: Model Factories will be hosted at SIMTech and ARTC, with the aim of being operational by the fourth quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Model Factories will be hosted at the Singapore Institute for Manufacturing Technology (SIMTech) and Advanced Remanufacturing and Technology Centre (ARTC).

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We aim to have them operational by the fourth quarter of this year.

sections.label: Startup and venture capital growth
sections.summary: Startups more than doubled from 22,000 in 2003 to 48,000 in 2015, with 220 venture capital deals worth over US$1 billion in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The total number of startups in Singapore more than doubled from 22,000 in 2003 to 48,000 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In 2015, there were 220 venture capital deals completed worth more than US$1 billion combined.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is compared to 26 deals worth US$80 million just five years ago.

sections.label: Startup SG umbrella branding
sections.summary: A new umbrella branding called "Startup SG" will be established to unify startup support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As a first step, therefore, we will establish a new umbrella branding known as "Startup SG" to unify our startup support schemes.

sections.label: Block 71 San Francisco launch pad
sections.summary: NUS Enterprise, SingTel Innov8 and SGInnovate jointly set up Block 71 in San Francisco as a launch pad for Singaporean tech startups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In the US, NUS Enterprise, SingTel Innov8 and SGInnovate jointly set up Block 71 at San Francisco as a launch pad for Singaporean tech startups.

sections.label: IE Singapore 2016 assistance figures
sections.summary: In 2016 IE Singapore assisted companies in over 37,000 cases, about 80% SMEs, and facilitated over 450 global projects, up from around 420 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In 2016, IE Singapore assisted companies in over 37,000 cases, with SMEs accounting for about 80% of them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: IE Singapore also helped companies facilitate over 450 projects globally in the same year, up from around 420 projects in 2015.

sections.label: IE Singapore Overseas Centres support
sections.summary: IE Singapore provides targeted in-market support through 37 Overseas Centres, many in emerging markets in Southeast Asia, China and India.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: IE Singapore provides highly targeted in-market support to our companies through its global network of 37 Overseas Centres, many of which are located in emerging markets in Southeast Asia, China and India.

sections.label: Consumer protection and errant retailers
sections.summary: The government takes firm action against errant retailers, amended the CPFTA in 2016 to empower SPRING, and cited the Volks Auto case.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: (In English): Let me now address Mr Lim Biow Chuan's question, which he submitted earlier to MTI, on how we can better protect our consumers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I wish to assure Mr Lim that we take a serious view of errant retailers who engage in unfair trading practices and will not hesitate to take firm action against them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We amended the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (CPFTA) in 2016 to empower SPRING with investigative and enforcement powers to take injunction action against errant businesses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Members may recall the recent case of parallel car importer Volks Auto.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: One of its employees was charged for criminal conspiracy to cheat its customers and sentenced to 10 years in jail.

sections.label: GRIT infrastructure talent programme
sections.summary: A new Professional Conversion Programme for Global-Ready Infrastructure Talent targets 300 individuals over five years, with on-the-job training and salary subsidy.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The Minister for Industry has announced how we will improve companies' access to private cross-border project financing.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: These initiatives will be complemented by the launch of a new Professional Conversion Programme for Global-Ready Infrastructure Talent (GRIT).

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We target to place and train 300 individuals over the next five years to develop a pipeline of talent in infrastructure project development.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: These candidates will receive on-the-job training for up to 18 months and they will gain relevant exposure to regional infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The programme will subsidise a part of the participant's salary.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Young Talent Programme
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Young Talent Programme offers overseas internships and work study, with over 500 students benefiting by end 2016, plus language courses payable with SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: For our youths, we have the SkillsFuture Young Talent Programme (YTP) that offers overseas internships and work study programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We are pleased to report that as at end of 2016, over 500 students have benefited from the YTP international experience.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Exposure is but one aspect of expanded horizons that we are all trying to cultivate.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I agree with Ms Sun that the ability to speak the native languages of emerging and growing markets is a definite asset.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: For those wishing to brush up on mother tongue languages or pick up new ones like Thai, Vietnamese, Japanese or Korean, SkillsFuture has various language courses to choose from and these can be paid for with the SkillsFuture Credit.

sections.label: Early stage of scheme
sections.summary: The scheme is in its early stage, contract sums must be reasonable for early-stage companies or SMEs, and SPRING will work with Government agencies to develop the model.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The answer is that it is in the early stage of the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Obviously, the contract sums have to be reasonable because they must be within the reach of whether an early-stage company or an SME.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: What we will do is, SPRING will work with the Government agencies, as I said, to develop the model, and then we will see how we go from there.

sections.label: Commission measures against anti-competitive companies
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Commission considers their interest when deciding measures against companies guilty of anti-competitive practices, and is confident CCS is addressing the issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Their interest also ought to matter and I hope the Commission can consider that when they look at what sort of measures ought to be instituted against companies found guilty of anti-competitive practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I am not able to comment on ongoing investigations, but I am confident that our colleagues at CCS are doing their best and addressing the issue as quickly as they can and as comprehensively as they can.

sections.label: Pricing and support for families
sections.summary: It is fully priced, support or subsidies are for families that need them more, and the approach relies on pricing without punitive pricing.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is fully priced and there is a reason for that, not unlike the discussion we had on other utilities and in the context of Singapore and in the context of this debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And then, when we offer the support or subsidies, these are for the families that need them more.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In general, we are relying on, first, the approach we take in pricing.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We have not gone down the path of punitive pricing, also because who is to say who is consuming too much and who is consuming appropriately?

sections.label: Setting thresholds involves many variables
sections.summary: Setting thresholds involves too many variables and starts to get the Government into areas that are quite fraught.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To set thresholds, there are too many variables involved, and it starts to get the Government into areas that are quite fraught.

sections.label: Water as proportion of costs
sections.summary: For most common commodities and products produced, water is quite small as a proportion of costs and should not warrant the same concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In general, if you look at most of the common commodities and products that are being produced, water, as a proportion of costs, is quite small and should not, therefore, warrant the same kind of concerns.
